rows: Adoption, touched-code migration, and compatibility labeling require coupled state across changes.
Command selection depends on the risk of the current task.
The explicit references to cw-gates and the build-topology file are directives to read them.
Reading code and call sites is required before producing the change.
Contributor provenance must remain consistent with commit authorship and credit metadata.
The required trust, data-loss, security, and accessibility guards are repository-specific.
Adding an abstraction is coupled to deleting its existing caller code.
Changing state must be derived from current repository, test, CI, and issue evidence rather than memory.
The required grep and predecessor lookup must precede adding the layer, with matching commit metadata.
Repository behavior and symbols must be searched before reviving or merging old work.
Committing and pushing are conditioned on prior verification, while destructive operations require current authorization.
The workflow requires reading, checking, fixing, grouping, and committing discovered work in sequence.
The edit's activity state must be observed before requesting and later making a commit.
Commit exclusion and gitignore handling require repository state, and secrets and outputs are unresolved concepts.
Repository visibility must be checked before deciding whether the push may expose sensitive details.
A prior check result determines whether the work may subsequently be pushed.
Compatibility identifiers may change only through an explicit migration, coupling identifier edits to migration work.
Model inputs, session events, presentation, and persisted logs must remain consistent across operations.
Remote pane identifiers must originate from discovery on the selected machine rather than inherited local state.
Remote state must be inspected before retrying after an ambiguous connection failure.
The explicit environment check must occur before any control command.
Pane availability and foreground state must be established before starting the agent.
The user-selected kind and installed-kind inspection determine the later start command.

Routing work to pane or agent commands depends on the current operation's purpose.

The role assignment directs the agent to act with the stated expertise.
